answer: Each identity binds to a single hardware authenticator that must respond to a random liveness signal inside a short window. One key can never serve two identities, so the bridge between a person and their on-chain account stays one-to-one. Every registration is a vertex in a device graph, and duplicate hardware fingerprints block the merge. A farm of 1,000 fake identities must buy 1,000 physical devices at roughly $30 each and catch every timing window, so the attacker's bill is $30,000 plus the labor of managing a thousand devices.
